items.title: ONU : la Tunisie appelle à rétablir la confiance dans le multilatéralisme et réaffirme son soutien à la Palestine
items.description: Prenant la parole a l'occasion de la 81e session de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies, le ministre tunisien des Affaires etrangeres, de la Migration et des Tunisiens a l'etranger, Mohamed Ali Nafti, a place la reforme du systeme multilateral au cœur de son intervention, appelant les etats a renforcer leur engagement en faveur du droit international et des principes de la Charte des Nations unies. Pour Tunis, le retablissement de la confiance dans l'ONU passe notamment par « une veritable determination » des etats a respecter le droit international, l'egalite souveraine entre les pays et le reglement pacifique des differends. La Tunisie plaide egalement pour une reforme « globale et profonde » des mecanismes de decision de l'organisation, avec une representation geographique plus equilibree ainsi que davantage de transparence et de responsabilite. Le ministre a apporte son soutien aux efforts engages dans le cadre de l'initiative « ONU80 », tout en estimant que celle-ci devait constituer une etape du processus de reforme et non son aboutissement. Tunis demande notamment que ce processus reste inclusif et preserve le caractere intergouvernemental de l'organisation. La Palestine au cœur du discours Une large partie de l'intervention a ete consacree a la situation au Proche-Orient. Mohamed Ali Nafti a denonce les violations des droits des Palestiniens et exhorte la communaute internationale a assumer ses responsabilites juridiques, morales et humanitaires. La Tunisie a condamne la poursuite de la colonisation en Cisjordanie ainsi que les politiques de « persecution, de famine et d'isolement » dans la bande de Gaza. Le ministre a egalement appele a garantir un acces humanitaire « sûr, urgent et durable » a l'enclave et a permettre aux agences des Nations unies d'y exercer leurs missions. Tunis a par ailleurs reaffirme son opposition a toute mesure visant a modifier le caractere historique, juridique et demographique de Jerusalem, citant notamment les deplacements forces de population, les demolitions de maisons et les attaques contre les lieux saints musulmans et chretiens. La Tunisie a egalement defendu le maintien de l'UNRWA, estimant que toute tentative de demantelement de l'agence ou d'affaiblissement de son mandat avant un reglement de la question des refugies palestiniens porterait atteinte au droit au retour. Le ministre a reaffirme le soutien de Tunis au droit des Palestiniens a etablir un etat independant et pleinement souverain, avec Al-Qods comme capitale. Des solutions politiques aux crises regionales Sur les autres crises du Moyen-Orient, la Tunisie a plaide pour la cessation des operations militaires et le retour au dialogue et aux negociations. Elle a rappele son attachement a la liberte de navigation et a la securite maritime, conformement au droit international. Concernant la Libye, Tunis a renouvele son soutien a une solution « libyenne-libyenne », fondee sur le dialogue et le consensus et preservant l'unite, la souverainete et l'integrite territoriale du pays. Le ministre a egalement exprime la solidarite de la Tunisie avec le Liban et condamne les violations repetees du cessez-le-feu, avant de denoncer les attaques contre le territoire et les ressources de la Syrie. Sur le Soudan, Tunis a appele a un cessez-le-feu immediat et permanent et a la reprise du processus de reconstruction. Elle a enfin soutenu les efforts visant a parvenir a un reglement politique durable de la crise au Yemen. L'Afrique et le developpement au premier plan Mohamed Ali Nafti a aussi insiste sur le potentiel humain et economique du continent africain, tout en soulignant les defis securitaires et economiques auxquels il reste confronte. La Tunisie a reaffirme son soutien au principe de « solutions africaines aux problemes africains » et a la reforme de l'Union africaine. Tunis souhaite egalement renforcer le partenariat entre l'ONU et l'Union africaine dans les domaines de la prevention des conflits, de la mediation, du maintien et de la consolidation de la paix et du developpement durable. Sur la migration, le ministre a defendu une approche globale prenant en compte les dimensions humaines et historiques du phenomene ainsi que ses causes profondes, notamment les conflits, la pauvrete, les disparites economiques et sociales et le manque d'opportunites. Il a rappele le refus de la Tunisie de devenir un pays de transit ou de destination pour les migrants irreguliers victimes des reseaux de traite. Justice climatique et reforme financiere La Tunisie a enfin plaide pour davantage de justice climatique et pour une reforme de l'architecture financiere internationale afin de faciliter l'acces des pays en developpement au financement. Tunis estime que les engagements des pays ayant la plus grande responsabilite historique dans les emissions doivent etre respectes. Le ministre a egalement evoque le developpement rapide de l'intelligence artificielle, estimant qu'il peut contribuer aux objectifs de developpement a condition de mettre en place une gouvernance mondiale equitable et d'eviter un approfondissement de la fracture numerique entre le Nord et le Sud. Sur le plan national, Mohamed Ali Nafti a affirme que la Tunisie poursuivrait le processus de reforme engage depuis le 25 juillet 2021 sous la direction du president Kaïs Saïed, en mettant en avant les droits et libertes, le developpement, l'investissement et la diversification des partenariats economiques. En conclusion, le ministre a souligne l'attachement de la Tunisie a l'ONU, qu'il a presentee comme « la maison de la legitimite internationale » et un cadre essentiel pour rechercher des solutions aux defis lies a la paix, a la securite et au developpement durable.

items.title: POWA calls for end to gendered attacks on Lordina Mahama, Samira Bawumia
items.description: The Progressive Organisation for Women’s Advancement (POWA) has called for an end to what it describes as gendered insults, personal attacks and mockery directed at First Lady Lordina Mahama and former Second Lady Samira Bawumia. POWA says the attacks go beyond ordinary partisan political exchanges and risk undermining the dignity and political agency of women in public life. In a statement issued on Tuesday, September 29, the organisation said women can belong to different political parties and hold opposing political views without being turned against one another. It said both Lordina Mahama and Samira Bawumia have occupied highly visible positions within Ghana’s political leadership and have platforms that could be used to advance issues affecting women, girls and vulnerable communities. “Those platforms should not become instruments of pitting women against one another,” POWA said. The organisation, however, stressed that its position should not be interpreted as shielding either woman from public scrutiny. It said women in political and public office must remain accountable for their words, actions and policies, but argued that accountability should be distinguished from humiliation, misogyny and personal attacks. POWA said political experiences of women are shaped not only by party affiliation but also by gender, class and access to institutional power. It argued that when women are encouraged to direct their political energy at one another, attention can shift away from structural inequalities that continue to limit women’s participation and influence. “When women divide, unequal power systems benefit,” the organisation said. It cited inadequate political representation, economic inequality, violence against women and girls, unequal access to opportunities, unpaid care responsibilities and barriers to decision-making among the challenges facing Ghanaian women. POWA said these issues require collective action across political and ideological lines. It therefore urged women’s rights organisations, women’s groups, civil society organisations and the wider public to reject what it described as the normalisation of gendered attacks against women in public life. POWA said Ghana’s prominent women in politics should identify areas of common interest and work towards a collective women’s agenda, even where they disagree politically. “Lordina Mahama need not agree with Samira Bawumia, and vice versa. Solidarity does not require political uniformity,” it said. “It requires recognising that advancing women’s collective development is bigger than any political party.” The organisation also called on women across Ghana to resist political divisions that, in its view, have historically weakened women’s collective bargaining power. It urged men who support gender equality to reject gendered political attacks and called on political actors across the political divide to demonstrate that political competition can coexist with respect for women’s dignity. POWA further appealed to Lordina Mahama and Samira Bawumia to consider leading a broader conversation on women’s political solidarity beyond party lines. The organisation said Ghana needs greater representation of women in decision-making and women who can disagree politically without undermining one another. “Ghana needs more women at the table. It needs women who can disagree without destroying one another,” POWA said. The statement was signed by POWA Founder, Dr Victoria Lakshmi Hamah. “Women’s power is people’s power,” the organisation said, urging Ghanaians not to allow partisan politics to prevent women from working together on issues affecting women and girls.

items.description: Lundi 28 septembre 2026, le ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens, Serigne Abdoul Ahad Ndiaye, a procédé à la mise en service de la deuxième phase du Train Express Régional, avec l’ouverture au public de la section reliant Diamniadio à l’Aéroport International Blaise Diagne (AIBD). Le TER dessert désormais directement la zone aéroportuaire de Diass. La nouvelle section représente environ 19 kilomètres de ligne ferroviaire en double voie électrifiée. Elle porte le linéaire total du TER à 55 kilomètres entre Dakar et l’AIBD. Ces 19 km supplémentaires, ont à coup sûr, un impact économique conséquent. Le TER, par sa capacité à réduire les distances, donc le temps, contribue progressivement à modifier la structure économique de la capitale sénégalaise. Dans une agglomération confrontée à des embouteillages récurrents, réduire la durée et l’incertitude des déplacements, revient en même temps, à élargir le taux de déplacements utiles, au profit des populations de la périphérie. Le TER permet ainsi aux habitants des zones desservies de se rapprocher plus facilement des pôles d’emploi, d’enseignement et de services, majoritairement concentrés à Dakar. Mais, l’enjeu dépasse la mobilité. Le TER peut, en effet, efficacement contribuer à modifier la géographie économique de Dakar. Diamniadio, déjà pensé comme un nouveau pôle urbain et économique bénéficie d’un raccordement ferroviaire supplémentaire qui la rapproche fortement de Dakar. L’amélioration de l’accessibilité accroît l’attractivité tout en stimulant les visions d’investissements immobiliers et commerciaux dans cette zone. Au fond, la réussite économique du TER ne se mesurera pas uniquement au nombre de voyageurs transportés au quotidien. S’il est accompagné d’une politique cohérente d’aménagement et d’attractivité économique, le TER peut devenir l’un des instruments de la transformation de Dakar, en une métropole plus connectée. O.BA

items.title: Zigx Foundation supports 50 vulnerable mothers in Akwapim North
items.description: The Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining is supporting 50 vulnerable mothers in Akwapim North as part of its 2026 Corporate Social Responsibility programme. The beneficiaries are members of the Nhyiramma Foundation Widows and Single Mothers Association, which provides vulnerable women with support, empowerment opportunities and a platform to rebuild their lives. As part of its 2026 Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme, Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining is supporting the 50 women as part of its commitment to improving the lives of women, children and underserved communities. For many mothers, the greatest challenge is not the absence of dreams, but the lack of resources to turn those dreams into reality. The initiative is more than a financial contribution. It is an investment in families, dignity and opportunity. “Every Child Deserves the Best” At the heart of Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining’s social intervention philosophy is a simple but powerful belief: every child deserves the best possible chance in life. The Foundation recognises that when a mother struggles to provide food, education, healthcare and basic necessities, her children are often the first to feel the impact. Supporting vulnerable mothers, therefore, becomes a way of supporting entire families and giving children a stronger foundation for the future. This latest intervention forms part of Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining’s broader record of community development and social investment, particularly in communities connected to its mining activities. Over the years, the Foundation has undertaken a number of initiatives aimed at improving access to education, healthcare and opportunities for vulnerable people. These include support towards the construction of schools, assistance with hospital bills for teenage mothers, and other interventions aimed at improving the welfare of people in mining communities. Its work reflects an approach to mining that goes beyond economic activity to include responsibility towards the people and communities within which mining takes place. Investing in mothers, investing in children The 50 women benefiting from this initiative are members of the Nhyiramma Foundation Widows and Single Mothers Association, which was established to provide vulnerable women with support, empowerment opportunities and a platform through which they can rebuild their lives. For many of these women, the responsibility of providing for their families rests heavily on their shoulders. The intervention by Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining is therefore expected to provide much-needed support while reinforcing the message that vulnerable women do not have to face their challenges alone. The initiative also aligns with Nhyiramma Foundation’s broader commitment to empowering women while creating better opportunities for the children and families who depend on them. A commitment beyond the cheque The partnership between the two foundations demonstrates the impact that can be achieved when organisations come together around a shared commitment to vulnerable communities. For Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining, the support is part of its continuing CSR commitment for 2026 and builds on its previous interventions in communities where it has worked. Its approach demonstrates that corporate social responsibility can be about more than donations. It can be about restoring dignity, creating opportunity and giving people the confidence to believe in a better tomorrow. For the 50 mothers receiving support, the gesture carries a message that goes beyond the value of the assistance: “You are seen. You matter. Your children matter. And your future is worth investing in.” As Zigx Foundation for Sustainable Mining continues its community interventions, its belief remains clear: “When we strengthen a mother, we strengthen a family; when we strengthen families, we strengthen communities; and when we invest in children, we invest in the future of Ghana.”

items.title: Drame de viol à Tunis | Il faut savoir raison garder
items.description: Une mineure de 15 ans se trouve actuellement dans un état critique en soins intensifs, dans un hôpital de la Tunis, souffrant de graves blessures et lésions internes. Elle a été victime d’un enlèvement, d’une séquestration et d’un viol collectif commis par plusieurs garçons de son âge, dans une maison du quartier de Mellassine, à la lisière ouest de la capitale. Les agresseurs auraient été identifiés et sont activement recherchés par la police. L’affaire suscite une vive émotion dans l’opinion et alimente un débat passionné et parfois violent sur les réseaux sociaux. Nous reproduisons ci-dessous le post facebook d’un médecin qui appelle à la raison et rappelle les fondements d’une société juste. Dr Kais Harzallah * Le drame vécu par cette jeune fille de 15 ans est effroyable. Toutes mes pensées vont d’abord vers elle, vers sa famille, et vers l’épreuve inimaginable qu’ils traversent. Mais l’horreur des faits rapportés ne doit pas nous faire renoncer à ce qui fonde une société juste. Je suis frappé par la rapidité avec laquelle les réseaux sociaux se transforment en tribunaux. Des visages sont exposés, des noms circulent, des culpabilités sont affirmées avant même que la justice n’ait établi précisément les faits. Certains réclament déjà la peine de mort. «Présumé innocent jusqu’à preuve du contraire» n’est pas une formule destinée à protéger les coupables. C’est un principe qui nous protège tous de l’arbitraire. Ce drame est aussi révélateur d’un malaise plus profond dans notre société : le regard devient superficiel, le jugement immédiat, la condamnation radicale. Les réseaux sociaux amplifient l’émotion jusqu’à parfois effacer la nuance, la prudence et la raison. Un fait divers, aussi grave et révoltant soit-il, doit être traité avec toute la rigueur de la justice, pas avec la vindicte d’une foule numérique. Protéger la victime, rechercher la vérité, établir les responsabilités et sanctionner les coupables avec toute la fermeté prévue par la loi : oui. Mais juger avant de savoir, exposer avant de prouver et condamner avant le procès : non. Une société se mesure aussi à sa capacité à rester juste lorsque l’émotion est à son comble. * Médecin de libre pratique. Tunis | Séquestrée et violée, une adolescente de 15 ans en réanimation L’article Drame de viol à Tunis | Il faut savoir raison garder est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Cameroun: la justice condamne Maître Alice Nkom
items.description: Maître Alice Nkom réagit à sa condamnation le lundi 21 septembre 2026 à un an de prison avec sursis et à une amende de 500.000 francs CFA, soit environ 760 euros. Maître Alice Nkom est poursuivie pour avoir refusé de déférer à une convocation du préfet de Douala et pour avoir brisé les scellés apposés sur les locaux du Redhac, du Réseau des défenseurs des droits humains d'Afrique centrale (Redhac) dont elle est aussi la présidente du conseil d'administration. Au micro d'Éric Topona, Maître Alice Nkom, connue au Cameroun et au-delà pour son engagement en faveur des droits des personnes LGBTQ+, a réagi à cette condamnation. Interview. Maître Alice Nkom : On m'a reproché d'avoir brisé les scellés que Monsieur le sous-préfet est venu apposer un lundi matin sur les portes et toutes les ouvertures du Redhac (le Réseau des défenseurs des droits humains d'Afrique centrale, dont je suis la présidente du conseil d'administration) et de rébellion parce que je n'aurais pas couru à la suite d'une convocation de Monsieur le préfet. La convocation a été envoyée à une adresse du quartier, convoqué en me disant : « Vous êtes dans tel quartier ». La convocation est arrivée à un moment où je ne pouvais plus y répondre. Dans un dossier comme celui-là qui se déroule à Douala, qui concerne Monsieur le ministre de l'Administration territoriale, les ordres au tribunal viennent de Yaoundé. Le jugement est rendu par Yaoundé. DW : Rappelons, Maître Alice Nkom, que le 6 décembre 2024, le ministre de l'Administration territoriale, Paul Atanga Nji, a suspendu cinq organisations non gouvernementales, dont le Redhac, pour une durée de trois mois. Il exige de la transparence sur l'identité de leurs bailleurs et sur la gestion de leurs fonds, invoquant des soupçons de blanchiment de capitaux et de financement du terrorisme. Où en est-on avec ces exigences ? ​ Alice Nkom : Nous existons à partir d'une loi internationale qui est au-dessus même de la Constitution et qui a été signée et ratifiée par le président de la République. Il aurait donc dû envoyer d'abord une équipe d'enquête pour regarder nos livres comptables et interroger tout le monde, avant de sanctionner. Mais je n'ai jamais vu d'équipe de Monsieur le ministre de l'Administration territoriale au Redhac en train d'enquêter sur quoi que ce soit. Nous avons le droit de recevoir des fonds, des financements extérieurs, parce que nous travaillons tous sur les droits de l'homme. Et le Cameroun respecte le principe de la hiérarchie des normes qui veut que la première loi ici au Cameroun, ce n'est pas la Constitution, c'est la convention internationale qui est la loi du Président de la République, avec les autres chefs d'État, qui va être signée et ratifiée par le Président de la République et qui va venir prendre la place en haut de la pyramide des lois du règlement du Cameroun. Source: Amp.dw.com L’article Cameroun: la justice condamne Maître Alice Nkom est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: National Assembly to translate laws into Igbo, Yoruba, Hausa, others
items.description: The National Assembly will soon deepen the digitisation of parliamentary records by translating Nigerian laws into Igbo, Hausa, Yoruba and other local languages to expand public access to legislative information. Mr Henry Nwawuba, the Executive Secretary, National Assembly Library Trust Fund, disclosed this while declaring open the 2026 National Assembly Library Week on Monday in Abuja. The event was themed, “Parliamentary Memory: Connecting Records, Legislation and the People.” Nwawuba said the three-day programme was designed as an annual platform to promote legislative research, access to information and effective utilisation of the resources of the National Assembly Library. He described the library as more than a collection of books, saying “it serves as the knowledge infrastructure of the legislature and a repository of parliamentary records.” He said the library was working to ensure that lawmakers, legislative aides, researchers and other stakeholders have access to authoritative parliamentary records, including Order Papers, Votes and Proceedings, Committee reports and Acts passed by the National Assembly. Nwawuba said the Trust Fund was investing in electronic repositories and upgrading of its E-Library, while developing a National Assembly Library mobile application to make legislative information more accessible to lawmakers, staff members, researchers and members of the public. He also announced plans for a Bills Tracker, which would enable users to follow bills and monitor their progress through the legislative process. According to him, the library is developing infographics, audiovisual materials and video explainers to simplify Bills, Acts and legislative procedures for Nigerians. He said the planned translation of laws into local languages would broaden access to legislative information and enable more citizens to understand laws that affect their daily lives. Nwawuba said the library would also organise public policy dialogues to deepen citizens’ participation in public hearings and create more opportunities for interaction among legislators, citizens, researchers and other stakeholders. He added that the initiatives were aimed at addressing inconsistencies in official parliamentary documents and the circulation of fake or unauthorised copies of National Assembly records. Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, urged lawmakers to make greater use of the library, particularly in an era of increasing misinformation, disinformation and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Akpabio, represented by Sen. Osita Ngwu, described the library as a critical link between evidence, knowledge and legislative decision-making and called for continued support for its development. The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, represented by the House Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, said legislative records were essential to understanding Nigeria’s legislative history and strengthening democratic governance. Tajudeen said the strength of a legislature should be measured not only by the laws it enacted, but also on how effectively it documented its activities, preserved institutional knowledge and made such information available to future generations. He said technology and artificial intelligence could improve legislative research, records preservation and access to information, but cautioned that their adoption must be guided by accuracy, security, professional judgment. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, said the National Assembly could not be truly independent if it lacked the capacity to generate, preserve, retrieve and authenticate its institutional knowledge and records. Ogunlana said the library had an important role as a bridge between parliamentary records, legislation and the people, stressing that Parliament could not be fully transparent if its records could not be found, understood and trusted. He identified the Order Paper, Votes and Proceedings and Hansard as key components of Nigeria’s democratic memory, explaining that the Order Paper provides the agenda for legislative business. The Clerk warned against the circulation of incomplete, outdated, altered or unauthorised Bills, Acts and other parliamentary documents, saying digital technology had made it possible for documents to be manipulated and circulated. He stressed that the integrity of an Act depended not merely on the existence of a document, but on the ability to establish which version was authentic, which was authoritative and the legal process through which it emerged. He noted that the continued widespread use of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, LFN 2004, highlighted the challenges of maintaining a current and authoritative consolidated body of federal legislation. He explained that the LFN 2004 reflected the laws covered by that revision exercise and was not automatically updated whenever a new Act was enacted. Ogunlana said the National Assembly must also strengthen cybersecurity, digital preservation, secure authentication, access controls, backup systems and staff members’ training as parliamentary records become increasingly digitised. He warned that while digitisation would make parliamentary information easier to access, search and disseminate, it could also expose records to cyberattacks, manipulation and impersonation of official sources. The Clerk said digital platforms must therefore be accessible and secure, while electronic records must be available, authentic and traceable. He said the National Assembly Library should evolve beyond being a repository where documents are kept to becoming an institution where parliamentary knowledge is preserved, authenticated and made accessible to lawmakers, researchers, journalists, civil society organisations, students and the wider public. The President of the Nigerian Library Association, Dr Lawal Umar, called for sustained investment in libraries and modern information technology to improve access to legislative information, while urging stronger collaboration between the National Assembly and state Houses of Assembly. The Secretary-General, Conference of Speakers of African Legislatures, Amb. Debo Oyewale, said African legislatures had much to learn from one another in building institutions capable of preserving legislative memory. (NAN) The post National Assembly to translate laws into Igbo, Yoruba, Hausa, others appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘I’ll look for him’ — Joao Felix eyes assist for Ronaldo’s 1,000th goal
items.description: Joao Felix has said he hopes to provide the assist for his Al Nassr and Portugal teammate, Cristiano Ronaldo’s 1,000th career goal. Ronaldo has scored 979 goals in 1,333 competitive appearances, leaving him 21 goals short of reaching the landmark. “I’ve thought about that,” Felix said in an interview with Diario AS . “When he’s one goal away, every time I get the ball I’ll look for him to see if I can give him the pass. “That goal will go down in soccer history, and being part of it would be a great moment.” Felix joined Al Nassr from Chelsea in 2025 and was named the Saudi Pro League’s player of the season for 2025-26, as the club won the league title for the first time in seven years. The triumph also gave Ronaldo his first major trophy since joining the Saudi club in late 2022. Felix said helping Ronaldo win the title was particularly significant for him, given the Portuguese forward’s status as an idol to his generation. “It’s something few people in soccer can say they’ve done,” he said. “I got to do it with the national team, and now at Al Nassr. “It’s an honor, honestly. We grew up watching Cristiano. He was our idol, someone we looked up to, and now I get to share these moments with him.” Reflecting on Al Nassr’s title success, Felix added: “Winning the league last year was especially meaningful. Being able to help Cristiano win the title he had been chasing since he arrived… “We have to enjoy it as much as we can because we know it won’t last forever. But while he’s here, we’ll be here too.” The post ‘I’ll look for him’ — Joao Felix eyes assist for Ronaldo’s 1,000th goal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ONU : l’Algérie appelle à réformer le système multilatéral et réaffirme ses positions sur la Palestine et le Sahara occidental
items.description: Le monde se trouve a « un carrefour », marque par la multiplication des conflits, la montee des tensions et le recul de la confiance entre les etats, a estime Ahmed Attaf devant l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies, le 28 septembre. Pour le ministre algerien des Affaires etrangeres, cette situation met en cause les fondements de l'ordre international etabli apres les deux guerres mondiales. Il a denonce la montee de l'unilateralisme, de la polarisation et des mesures coercitives, ainsi que ce qu'il a presente comme une application selective du droit international. « Le danger ne reside pas seulement dans le declenchement des guerres, mais aussi dans la normalisation et l'acceptation de la guerre elle-meme », a-t-il declare. Alger plaide pour une reforme profonde du Conseil de securite Pour restaurer la confiance dans le systeme multilateral, l'Algerie estime que la reforme doit commencer au sein meme des Nations unies. Ahmed Attaf a appele a renforcer le role et l'autorite de l'Assemblee generale et a engager une reforme « profonde » du Conseil de securite afin de le rendre plus representatif, equitable et efficace. Alger demande notamment une representation africaine permanente au Conseil de securite, dotee de pouvoirs complets, au nom de la correction de ce qu'il qualifie d'« injustice historique » envers le continent africain. Le ministre a egalement insiste sur la necessite de mettre fin a la selectivite et aux « deux poids, deux mesures » dans l'application du droit international. Soutien reaffirme aux Palestiniens La situation au Proche-Orient a occupe une place importante dans l'intervention algerienne. Ahmed Attaf a denonce la poursuite des violences contre les civils palestiniens et estime que leur situation ne devait pas devenir une realite « normalisee » aux yeux de la communaute internationale. L'Algerie a reaffirme son soutien « plein et inconditionnel » aux droits « legitimes et inalienables » du peuple palestinien , notamment son droit a etablir un etat independant et pleinement souverain, avec Al-Qods comme capitale. Le ministre a egalement condamne les attaques israeliennes contre plusieurs pays de la region, citant notamment la Syrie et le Liban, et appele a la desescalade ainsi qu'au respect de la souverainete et de l'integrite territoriale des etats. Le Sahara occidental, « question de decolonisation » Ahmed Attaf a ensuite reaffirme le soutien de l'Algerie au droit du peuple du Sahara occidental a l'autodetermination. Il a salue l'organisation de negociations directes entre le Maroc et le Front Polisario sous l'egide des Nations unies, avec l'assistance des etats-Unis, tout en appelant les deux parties a s'engager « de bonne foi » dans le processus. Alger estime que toute solution doit rester inscrite dans le cadre des references pertinentes des Nations unies et de la doctrine de l'organisation en matiere de decolonisation. Le ministre a mis en garde contre toute tentative de marginaliser les parties qu'il considere comme detentrices de droits legitimes. L'Algerie a egalement defendu le maintien de la question du Sahara occidental dans le cadre de la decolonisation, rejetant l'idee que le passage du temps puisse transformer une situation qu'elle considere comme imposee en fait juridique. Sahel et Libye : securite, developpement et dialogue Sur le Sahel, Ahmed Attaf a defendu une approche combinant securite et developpement. Selon lui, la lutte contre le terrorisme ne peut etre dissociee de la pauvrete et de la marginalisation, tandis que la stabilite securitaire constitue une condition du developpement. L'Algerie a reaffirme sa disponibilite a soutenir les pays de la region et a appuyer les solutions politiques favorisant la stabilite, tout en insistant sur le respect de la souverainete des etats et des choix de leurs peuples. Concernant la Libye, Alger a renouvele son soutien a une solution politique « pacifique, globale et dirigee par les Libyens ». Le ministre a appele a mettre fin aux ingerences etrangeres et a parvenir a l'unification des institutions libyennes. L'Algerie defend une cooperation africaine renforcee Le ministre a egalement presente le developpement durable comme indissociable de la paix et de la securite. Il a mis en avant les progres revendiques par l'Algerie dans la mise en œuvre des Objectifs de developpement durable et appele a renforcer l'integration africaine. Ahmed Attaf a enfin plaide pour que le continent africain ne reste pas a la marge de la revolution technologique. Il a appele a investir dans les competences scientifiques et numeriques africaines et a mettre en place une reglementation internationale « equilibree et responsable » de l'intelligence artificielle, garantissant un acces equitable a ses benefices. En conclusion, le chef de la diplomatie algerienne a resume son appel autour d'une meme exigence : restaurer la confiance en faisant correspondre les paroles et les actes, en appliquant le droit international de maniere egale et en faisant des Nations unies un espace ou la diplomatie et le multilateralisme retrouvent pleinement leur place.

items.title: Can the Polls Possibly Be Right?
items.description: When this year began, the Democrats were heavy underdogs to take back the Senate in the midterms. The task would require not only toppling Susan Collins in Maine but also winning at least five states that voted for Donald Trump in 2024, while holding on to all of the party’s existing seats. The realistic best-case scenario seemed to be a replay of the so-called blue-wave 2018 election, during Trump’s first term, in which Democrats took back the House but the Senate remained in Republican hands. To gain control of the upper chamber, Democrats would need an incredible stroke of luck. They might have gotten one. Trump’s decision to start a war with Iran, and the resulting spike in oil prices, shifted the boundaries of the politically possible. A year ago, Trump was merely unpopular: By about 11 percentage points, more people disapproved of his performance than approved of it, according to The New York Times ’ polling average . He would kill for such good numbers today. Seven months into the Iran debacle, his disapproval margin has widened to 23 percentage points—worse than his numbers in the immediate aftermath of January 6. Predictably, Trump’s unpopularity is spilling out into the midterm races. Recent polls have been almost unbelievably positive for Democrats. Troy Jackson is ahead, albeit narrowly, in Maine. Abdul El-Sayed has a modest lead in Michigan, and Democrats have even bigger advantages in the swing states of Georgia and North Carolina, both of which Trump won in 2024. Most astonishing, Democratic candidates are in position to pull off upsets in Alaska, Texas, Ohio, and Iowa, which all went for Trump by more than 10 percentage points. Republican incumbents look beatable even in Kansas, where Trump won by 16, and Nebraska, where he won by 20. As a result, in prediction markets, Democrats’ chances of winning the Senate are now more than 60 percent. [ Read: The supporters urging Trump to declare martial law for the midterms ] If the election in November plays out as the polls are suggesting it will, Republicans will have their leader to thank—and themselves. With few exceptions, Republican candidates have created almost no distance from the president. Indeed, candidates in must-win red states, including Jon Husted of Ohio and Ken Paxton of Texas, gave speeches at the same Republican midterm convention where Trump led the audience in a pledge to the “greatest president in the history of the United States.” Democrats, by contrast, have been relatively disciplined. Candidates with a track record of winning over moderate voters were successfully recruited in Alaska, North Carolina, Iowa, Maine, Ohio, and Nebraska, and primary voters in those states were wise enough to nominate them (or, in Nebraska’s case, nominate someone who promised to drop out in favor of an independent with a better chance to win). Even where candidates with narrower appeal were nominated, as in Texas and Michigan, they have been cannily pivoting away from their unpopular progressive stances. If Democrats won both the House and Senate, they would be able to put a real check on Trump’s ambitions for the rest of his presidency. His legislative agenda would be at their mercy. Democrats would use their control of committees in both chambers to launch extensive investigations into government wrongdoing and corruption. And Trump’s judicial nominees would need to make a convincing case that they’d be impartial judges, not dogmatic loyalists. A Democratic sweep would have ripple effects beyond 2026. Each Senate seat that the party picks up this year makes winning in 2028 that much easier. If the electoral environment remains favorable for Democrats two years from now, the party could feasibly pick up seats in Wisconsin and North Carolina. Suddenly, a stronger, more diverse, and more nationally competitive Democratic Party is at least imaginable. All of this analysis hinges on assuming that the polls are accurate. For three presidential elections in a row, pollsters have badly underestimated Trump’s appeal. And in general, as the Republican pollster Patrick Ruffini has pointed out , the pro-Democratic bias tends to be largest in red states, the very ones that Democrats need in order to take back the Senate. Moreover, not every poll has looked good for Democrats—a recent New York Times and Siena College survey found Collins ahead in Maine, though Jackson leads in most polls. [ Read: The Republicans are bolting from Trump ] The good news for Democrats is that Trump-era midterm polls have been highly accurate on average, much more so than in presidential-election years. That’s because the midterm electorate includes fewer of the low-trust, politically disengaged voters who are so hard for pollsters to reach and disproportionately turn out when Trump is on the ballot. Even if the polls are accurate, things could change between now and November 3. Perhaps Trump could find a way to credibly declare victory in Iran. Individual Democratic candidates could become embroiled in scandal. Republican candidates could figure out how to distance themselves from Trump down the stretch. Yet the likeliest scenario at the moment, hard as it is to believe, is Democrats winning multiple Senate seats in states that Trump won in 2024 by double digits, taking control of both houses of Congress, earning the right to be involved in the legislative process, and providing a meaningful check on Trump’s power. The remarkable fact is that Republicans are now the party hoping for a stroke of good luck.

items.title: El Salvador’s Mass Incarceration of U.S. Deportees
items.description: A na paced near the arrivals terminal of the San Salvador airport, eyeing the door where deportees from the United States are released. She was there on a sweltering day in May to pick up her son, who had been detained in Texas and deported. She would drive him home, she decided, and cook him dinner. They would figure out what to do next. But when a group of men walked out wearing ICE-issued sweatsuits, their shoelaces removed from their shoes, her son wasn’t among them. She approached a police officer, who searched his name on a tablet. “He’s being taken to prison,” he told her. Ana, who spoke with me on the condition that I not use her real name or her son’s name, was confused. Her son, 25, did not face charges in either the U.S. or El Salvador. Ana got the name of the police station where her son had been taken. From there, she was told, he would be transferred to a maximum-security prison that has become infamous in El Salvador for the number of prisoners who have died in custody. She sped to the station and begged an officer to let her inside. “You can have five minutes with him,” the officer said, “but try to control yourself.” The officer returned with her son, who was wearing a white shirt and handcuffs. He looked handsome, Ana thought. He had been living in the United States for four years, having fled El Salvador after being physically attacked by both gangs and police officers, according to his asylum application. Ana started crying as she hugged him. She promised to deliver food to the prison. “This isn’t going to be forever,” he said as the officer escorted him away. She hasn’t seen or heard from him since. A year and a half ago, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a 31-year-old Salvadoran man, was deported to El Salvador and detained in a maximum-security mega-prison known as CECOT. Abrego’s deportation, which was in violation of legal orders, prompted a public backlash and a federal judge’s intervention; he was ultimately returned to the United States. But as public attention has shifted elsewhere, El Salvador has continued imprisoning deportees sent from the United States, including many who have not been charged with any crime. They have disappeared into the country’s black hole of a correctional system, where lawyers can’t locate them. Even though the U.S. is aware of these extrajudicial detentions, it has dramatically increased the number of people it sends to El Salvador. On most days, the U.S. flies deportees to the San Salvador airport—after which some vanish. One person with knowledge of the deportation flights in El Salvador told me that about four people from every flight of 120 passengers are jailed. Some deportees said that even more people on their flights had been detained. The United States has roughly doubled its number of deportations to El Salvador in the first half of this year. From January to June, 9,829 deportees arrived on at least 83 flights, according to El Salvador’s migration ministry. The scale of the ongoing detention of deportees has not been previously reported. [ Read: How the Trump administration flipped on Kilmar Abrego Garcia ] When deportation flights land, Salvadoran officials board the planes and read a handful of names from a list. Those people are escorted from the plane in handcuffs and taken to waiting police vehicles. On the airport tarmac as passengers disembark, security officials pull aside other deportees who have been judged to look like gang members. The jailed deportees remain in Salvadoran detention, unable to speak with their attorney or family, and usually without being told which crimes they’re accused of committing. Many detained deportees have been sent to CECOT. Others are transferred between other prisons across the country. The government won’t confirm for family members where people are detained or whether they are even still alive. At least five deportees from the U.S. have died in custody, according to Cristosal, a Salvadoran human-rights organization. In three of those cases, the group said, the bodies showed signs of violence or torture. The Trump administration claims to have no responsibility for what goes on after deportees are sent to El Salvador. “Once an alien is removed from the United States, the alien is no longer in ICE custody or under ICE’s purview,” an ICE spokesperson wrote to me in a statement responding to a question about deportees being detained. For the past three months, Ana has made frequent trips to the prison where she believes her son is detained to leave care packages of soap, food, and clothes. Officers take those packages but do not offer any information about her son’s legal status. She requested and received a signed document from the country’s justice department that says that her son “HAS NO CRIMINAL HISTORY.” (My search of public records likewise failed to reveal any history of charges in the United States.) He has been assigned a public defender, who has not been able to meet with him. The attorney told Ana that her son has been charged with “illicit association”—the generic charge leveled against prisoners who have been detained as part of the government’s crackdown on gangs. It carries a maximum sentence of 60 years. “I don’t know if I’ll ever see him again,” Ana told me. I n 2022, El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, announced a “state of exception” that would allow his government to round up large numbers of suspected gang members and jail them without charges. It was initially meant to last 30 days, but it has been extended for more than four years. In that time, Bukele’s government has made more than 90,000 arrests, representing about 2 percent of the country’s adult population. Some of those people—almost all boys and men—have been part of mass trials in which hundreds of inmates are convicted at the same time over videoconference, with no publicly available evidence presented. Some inmates are as young as 12. The crackdown has led to a significant decline in the nation’s homicide rate and made Bukele into a popular figure not only in parts of El Salvador but also across much of Latin America. It has also made him a close ally of the Trump administration, which sees Bukele as an important part of a rightward shift across the region. But Bukele’s greatest gift to Donald Trump was his offer in 2025 to accept criminal deportees from the United States and incarcerate them in his country’s prisons in exchange for a fee. (The U.S. paid El Salvador nearly $5 million.) Bukele called it an opportunity for the U.S. to “outsource part of its prison system.” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the deal was “an act of extraordinary friendship.” The first flights of Venezuelan deportees landed in San Salvador in March of last year. That month, then–Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem visited CECOT, saying in a video as she stood before a prison cell full of silent, shirtless inmates that “if you come to our country illegally, this is one of the consequences you could face.” Bukele boasted about the cruelty prisoners endure in his detention facilities, posting photos and videos of prisoners being marched with their heads shaved. But it quickly became clear that many of the deportees the United States was sending to El Salvador, including Abrego Garcia, were not hardened criminals. The U.S. stopped deporting non-Salvadorans to El Salvador last April. It no longer needs to; it is now sending deportees to roughly 30 other “third country” destinations, many of them much farther away, including Liberia and South Sudan. In Congress and among NGOs, the focus has shifted away from human-rights violations in Salvadoran prisons. [ Read: El Salvador’s exceptional prison state ] But El Salvador never stopped incarcerating deportees, and now it is detaining its own nationals. I spoke with nine families whose relatives have been deported since as early as March 2025 and remain in detention. Some learned of their loved one’s whereabouts only when they were spotted in the background of Salvadoran-government videos and photos. Dual U.S. citizens visiting the country of their birth have also become caught up in the crackdown, some of them apparently detained because they had tattoos that were deemed suspicious by Salvadoran authorities. In January, one Salvadoran man was deported from the United States even after a judge ordered a hold on his removal based on the United Nations Convention Against Torture, a case not unlike Abrego Garcia’s. He was detained upon arrival in El Salvador. His lawyer wrote in a July court filing that “Salvadoran authorities have transferred Petitioner between prisons, and his family has not been provided information regarding his current location, his condition, or whether he is alive.” Gustavo Villatoro, El Salvador’s minister of justice and public security, has released the mug shots of some deportees who he says are gang members who must be detained. “In El Salvador, deported gang members do not return to the streets: here they are terrorists and go straight to jail to answer for their actions in the criminal case against the international MS13,” Villatoro wrote on X in May. Last month, a passenger at the San Salvador airport posted a video on TikTok that showed police escorting deportees off the tarmac in handcuffs. Irvin Jeovanny Quintanilla García was deported from Texas in March 2025. But the Salvadoran government wouldn’t confirm for his family where he had been sent or whether he was in the country at all. He had not been convicted of a crime in the United States or in El Salvador. “It was like he had disappeared,” Luis Quintanilla, Irvin’s brother, told me. Months later, Luis saw his brother in two frames of a video recorded inside a Salvadoran prison, eating lunch and standing in a prison workshop. He wore a white long-sleeve shirt and a yellow baseball cap. The family hired a Salvadoran lawyer to figure out whether Irvin faced any charges. But the Salvadoran attorney general’s office would not respond to him. The lawyer then contacted the Inter-American Court of Human Rights, a judicial body that seeks to resolve disputes across the Americas, which wrote an official letter to El Salvador’s government requesting information about Quintanilla’s case. It wrote similar letters on behalf of five other deported detainees. In each case, the Salvadoran government responded cryptically that the deportees are being held as part of a “collaboration and sovereign cooperation” between the United States and El Salvador, and that El Salvador is acting only as a “receptor state” while the U.S. maintains “penal jurisdiction” over the cases. Neither the U.S. nor El Salvador has explained what that means. Out of desperation, Quintanilla’s mother, who was living in the United States at the time of Irvin’s deportation, returned to El Salvador to search for him. She is now dropping off her own care packages once a month at the prison where she believes he is being held. “But we don’t know for sure that he’s there,” Irvin’s brother said. “They won’t tell us anything.” S arah Bishop, a professor at Baruch College, serves as an expert witness in the asylum hearings of Salvadorans. Since the start of the state of exception in 2022, she has interviewed the family members of 30 Salvadoran men detained after their deportation. Only one has been released. In a recent case, she told a U.S. immigration judge that based on a man’s criminal record, tattoos, and history of interactions with MS-13, he was “exceedingly likely” to be jailed by Salvadoran police if he was sent back. The judge denied the case, and the man was deported this past summer. Bishop spoke with the man’s family a few days afterward. As she predicted, the man had been jailed upon arrival. Although it’s difficult to know the exact criteria that Salvadoran security officials are using to determine which deportees to detain, at least some of that information appears to be coming from the United States. In 2014, the two countries signed a memorandum of cooperation that would allow the U.S. to share the criminal history of deportees. At the time, ICE said that it was meant to help El Salvador “categorize and monitor repatriated criminals for domestic purposes.” But under Bukele, the information is being used to justify detaining deportees, even if they have no outstanding arrest warrants. [ Read: What the deported Venezuelans went through in El Salvador ] When Bukele has been accused of jailing innocent people or overreaching in his crackdown, he has pointed to the country’s security gains. “I don’t care if they call me a dictator. I’d rather be called a dictator than see Salvadorans being killed in the streets,” he said last year. The families of the imprisoned deportees continue crisscrossing the country to locate their loved ones. Some have formed a WhatsApp group called “Families in search of justice” where they exchange information about their children’s cases or whereabouts. But there is rarely new information. So instead, the families vent their anger and appeal to a higher power. “They will pay for every innocent person who suffered at their hands,” one mother wrote earlier this month. “I pray for a miracle from God,” another responded.

items.title: Ouagadougou: près de 86 kilogrammes de cannabis saisis
items.description: La police nationale du Burkina Faso affirme, dans un écrit ce mardi 29 septembre 2026 sur son réseau social Facebook, avoir démantelé un réseau de trafic et de vente de drogue à Ouagadougou et a saisi près de 86 Kilogramme de cannabis. «L’Unité Anti-Drogue de la Direction de la Police Judiciaire (DPJ) a, dans le cadre de la lutte contre le trafic de stupéfiants, mis un terme aux activités illicites d’un réseau de trafic et de vente de cannabis à Ouagadougou. En effet, dans un contexte marqué par l'insécurité et la prolifération des stupéfiants sur l’ensemble du territoire national, elle a intensifié ses actions de lutte contre le trafic et la consommation de drogues dans la ville de Ouagadougou. Ce qui a conduit au démantèlement de ce réseau bien structuré dont les membres s'adonnaient au trafic, à la vente et à la consommation de stupéfiants, de boissons frelatées, de cigarettes de contrebande et de produits psychotropes. Relativement au mode opératoire du groupe, ses membres, qui sont impliqués à divers degrés, effectuaient leur approvisionnement depuis un pays voisin. La marchandise était ensuite acheminée vers Ouagadougou par l’intermédiaire de véhicules de transport en commun ou de véhicules personnels. Une fois à Ouagadougou, elle était stockée avant d’être vendue ou redistribuée à la clientèle. Il est à noter qu’une partie était destinée à des revendeurs et grossistes opérant sur différents sites d’orpaillage à l’intérieur du pays, notamment Boromo et Poura dans la province des Balé, Zanténé dans la province du Sanguié, Sabcé dans la province du Bam, et Mogré et Bittou dans la province du Boulgou. items.title: Ferme géante Baladna Algérie : le virologue Yahia Chebloune appelle à la vigilance
items.description: Les premiers troupeaux de vaches américaines pour la ferme géante Baladna Algérie sont attendus à Adrar en novembre prochain. Le virologue algérien Yahia Chebloune, qui fait partie des membres du Haut conseil scientifique de la communauté algérienne à l’étranger qui ont été reçus par le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune dimanche 27 septembre, appelle déjà à une vigilance maximale afin d'éviter l’entrée avec ces cheptels de maladies animales. Les premières vaches américaines attendues à Adrar le 25 novembre Le projet Baladna est un investissement intégré de 3,5 milliards de dollars lancé avec le groupe laitier qatari pour la production de lait dans la wilaya d’Adrar, dans le sud de l’Algérie. Le projet comprend une ferme géante de 270 000 vaches, la production de fourrages sur 219 000 hectares et la réalisation d’une usine de production de lait en poudre d’une capacité de 193 000 tonnes par an. Le coût de l’investissement, engagé par le Fonds national d'investissement (FNI) et le Qatari Baladna, est estimé à 3,5 milliards de dollars. La semaine passée, Baladna El Djazaïr a annoncé que tout est fin prêt sur place, (l'eau, le fourrage, les hangars, les systèmes de climatisation, les routes et les équipes de travailleurs) pour accueillir les premières vaches importées des États-Unis dès le 25 novembre prochain. Un accord avait été conclu avec des fournisseurs américains pour la livraison de 30 000 vaches. Le nombre de bovins qui arriveront le 25 novembre n’a pas été précisé, mais vu le nombre que la méga-ferme est appelée à abriter à terme, le virologue algérien Yahia Chebloune a insisté sur l'extrême vigilance qui doit accompagner l’entrée des vaches importées sur le territoire national. Le professeur Yahia Chebloune appelle à la vigilance M. Chebloune, chercheur à l’université de Grenoble et à l'institut français de recherche en agronomie (INRAE) et directeur de PAVAL Lab (Laboratoire Pathogénèse et Vaccination Lentivirales), figure parmi les membres du Haut conseil des scientifiques algériens à l'étranger, reçus dimanche par le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune. “ Avec un tel grand nombre de vaches, le risque grandit aussi. Sur un petit cheptel, on peut arrêter la contamination, mais avec 270 000 vaches, s’il y a des contaminations, ça va être une catastrophe ”, a mis en garde le virologue dans des déclarations rapportées par La Patrie News. Pour réduire le risque, préconise-t-i, il faut disposer de vaccins “ fabriqués et connus ici ” afin de pouvoir maîtriser les éventuelles maladies de ces cheptels. Le chercheur a expliqué que le risque n’est pas seulement pour la santé des bovins, mais aussi pour les consommateurs puisque ces vaches vont produire du lait destiné à la consommation humaine. “ Il faut arriver à être sûr à 100 % d'avoir un lait sain ”, a-t-il insisté. L’article Ferme géante Baladna Algérie : le virologue Yahia Chebloune appelle à la vigilance est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Tinubu departs Paris for Nigeria
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has ended his working vacation and has already departed Paris, France, for the homeward journey to Nigeria. President Tinubu’s aircraft is expected to touch down at Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, later this evening. The Nigerian leader chose to fly to Lagos first to honour the memory of Chief MKO Abiola, the martyr of Nigeria’s democratic struggle. On Independence Day, the President will attend the premiere of a movie honouring Abiola, the winner of the June 1993 election, at the Wole Soyinka National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. While in Lagos, President Tinubu will also hold strategic meetings with political leaders and associates over several days in preparation for the 2027 elections. The President departed Abuja on August 30 for the working vacation. He spent one week in London before heading for Paris. While in Paris, he attended a private dinner with President Emmanuel Macron. He also met with business leaders, including Mr Vincent Bolloré of the Bolloré Group, whose media and digital interests include Canal+, MultiChoice and Universal Music Group. On Monday, he also met with the Chairman of First Holdings, Femi Otedola. Last week, President Tinubu witnessed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ogun State Government and DP World to build a Gateway deep seaport in Ogun Waterside and create a Blue Marine Economic Zone in the area. DP World, one of the world’s leading ports and logistics operators, plans to invest $7 billion for the seaport and the economic zone. President Tinubu will return to Abuja after his political engagements in Lagos. The post Tinubu departs Paris for Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ligue pro: Teungueth rêve d’un « back-to-back » inédit
items.description: Champion sortant, Teungueth Fc sera sans nul doute l’équipe la plus attendue de la saison, et celle à battre. En conservant sa couronne, le club, âgé de seulement 16 ans, enrichirait un palmarès déjà élogieux et inscrirait durablement son nom dans les annales du football sénégalais. Mais se hisser au sommet est une chose, s’y maintenir en est une autre. Le manque de régularité reste le mal des clubs sénégalais, en particulier des champions sortants. Sacré en 2025, le Jaraaf a calé à la 7e place la saison dernière. Teungueth Fc a connu le même sort en 2024-2025, bataillant jusqu’à la dernière journée pour se sauver (11e). Génération Foot, titrée la saison précédente, avait, elle aussi, fini 11e en 2023-2024. L’entraîneur des Grenats, Pape Boubacar Gadiaga, décrit d’ailleurs un championnat qui manque de logique, où le dernier peut battre le premier chez lui, et avec la manière. La saison écoulée, Ajel, alors leader, avait buté sur des adversaires à sa portée : nul vierge à domicile contre la lanterne rouge, Cambérène, défaites face au Stade de Mbour (0-1) et aux Hlm (0-3). Loin de ce fatalisme, Teungueth Fc a des arguments pour aller chercher un deuxième titre consécutif, le quatrième de son histoire après 2021, 2024 et 2026. Le club phare de Rufisque dispose d’un effectif étoffé, fruit d’un recrutement soigné. Une dizaine de joueurs ont rejoint les « Bleu et Blanc », parmi lesquels le jeune gardien Gorgui Diop et le milieu Souleymane Dieng, venus d’Ajel, les ailiers Albert Bougazelli et Ibou Aïdara, de Wally Daan Fc, le défenseur Mbaye Ndiaye, ancien du Jaraaf, ou encore Patrick Basse, arrivé de Guédiawaye Fc. Malick Daf peut aussi compter sur une défense de fer, incarnée par Papa Abdoulaye Dieng : 25 clean sheets en 29 matchs, et seulement 5 des 6 buts encaissés par le club la saison passée. Malgré le départ de Maguette Diop pour Bourges FcC, en France, l’équipe garde des joueurs de qualité comme Raphaël Ndong, le Gambien Ebrima Seckan, Mame Birame Diaw ou Ben Habib Diouf. Technicien au fort tempérament, Malick Daf se décrit comme un « homme de défi » et un « gagneur ». « Qui connaît Malick Daf sait qu’il est un vainqueur, un champion. Je suis ici pour gagner, pour essayer de hisser le club au plus haut niveau », confiait-il au Soleil à son arrivée. Après le Jaraaf en 2025 et Teungueth en 2026, il peut viser une troisième étoile d’affilée, qui porterait son palmarès à cinq titres. Qualifié pour le second tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions, où il affrontera la Colombe sportive du Dja et Lobo (Cameroun), Teungueth Fc entamera le championnat à domicile contre l’US Ouakam, avec un capital confiance intact et une préparation réussie. Selon son entraîneur, il ne manque plus que les automatismes, notamment dans la liaison entre le milieu et l’attaque. Par Mohamed DIENE (Correspondant à Rufisque)

items.title: Pakistan produce stunning comeback to secure 2-2 draw against Philippines in FIFA ASEAN Cup
items.description: Ali Akbar Khan scored his first international goal to spark a stirring fightback as Pakistan came from two goals down to hold the Philippines to a 2-2 draw in the FIFA ASEAN Cup on Tuesday, with Abdul Samad Arshad netting the equaliser. Nolberto Solano’s men had suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat in their Division I Group ‘B’ opener against Thailand, but they showed remarkable resilience and powers of recovery in a gritty performance. The draw delivered Pakistan their first goals and first point in their debut appearance in a FIFA competition. The result carried extra significance given the ranking gap — Pakistan, ranked 198th in the world, faced a Philippines side sitting 135th–136th — a difference of more than 60 places. Pakistan were put under early pressure by the higher-ranked hosts of the group stage fixture at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium. The defence dealt with a barrage of crosses, with Mohibullah Afridi putting his body on the line to turn a low cross behind for a corner, while goalkeeper Yousuf Butt denied André Leipold in a one-on-one situation. The Philippines broke the deadlock with a scrappy goal in the 24th minute. Mohibullah, on the line, turned a header onto the bar, but Sandro Reyes reacted quickest to the rebound and bundled it home. Pakistan responded with their first real chance minutes later when Ali Akbar broke through only to see his effort saved by a diving Kevin Ray Mendoza. The miss proved costly. Two minutes past the half-hour mark, a handball by Mohammad Fazal inside the box led to a penalty. Bjørn Kristensen sent Yousuf the wrong way from the spot to make it 2-0. The Philippines continued to press, with centre-back Haris Zeb blocking a diving header and Yousuf called into action again. Late in the half, Pakistan countered but Alamgir Ghazi shot high from distance. Solano made two changes at the break, introducing Ali Agha and Hayyan Khattak for Alamgir and Umar Nawaz. The adjustments paid immediate dividends. Two minutes into the second half, skipper Abdullah Iqbal found Ali Akbar on the left. The forward weaved past a defender and slotted the ball between Mendoza’s legs for his maiden international goal. Pakistan kept pushing. Hayyan shot wide moments later, and on the hour mark a cutback failed to reach Ali Akbar. The equaliser soon arrived: Abdul Samad Arshad won the ball on the right, drove into the box, cut onto his left foot and fired past a helpless Mendoza for his second international goal, making it 2-2. Solano later handed international debuts to left-back Abdul Rehman and Abdul Samad Khan, replacing Fazal and Ali Uzair, as Pakistan continued to attack. At the other end, Mohibullah produced another vital block from point-blank range on a Philippines counter. With Pakistan fans in the stands urging them on, the Green Shirts pressed for a winner but the Philippines held firm. The hard-earned point keeps Pakistan’s campaign alive in Group ‘B’ ahead of their final fixture against Vietnam.

items.title: Cameroun/ Douala : 80 chercheurs planchent sur l’avenir des forêts du Bassin du Congo
items.description: © DR Du 23 au 25 septembre 2026 à Douala, une soixantaine de jeunes chercheurs et une vingtaine de seniors venus de toute la sous-région ont partagé leurs travaux sur la biodiversité, l'agroforesterie, le carbone et la gouvernance forestière, dans le cadre de la One Forest Vision. Trois jours pour mobiliser la science au service de la gestion durable. Douala s'est muée en capitale scientifique des forêts d'Afrique centrale. Du 23 au 25 septembre 2026, la capitale économique a accueilli une soixantaine de jeunes chercheurs et une vingtaine de chercheurs seniors venus de toute la sous-région pour débattre de l'avenir des forêts du Bassin du Congo. Au programme : biodiversité, agroforesterie, carbone, sciences du bois et gouvernance. Trois jours d'échanges intenses visant à mieux mobiliser la science au service de la gestion durable de la deuxième forêt tropicale mondiale, poumon vert crucial face aux enjeux climatiques. Temps fort de cette rencontre, un dialogue inédit avec le secteur privé a été organisé pour rapprocher recherche fondamentale et réalités opérationnelles de l'exploitation et de la conservation. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre de la coopération scientifique entre la France et l'Afrique centrale, portée par la One Forest Vision, l'initiative lancée pour renforcer la recherche collaborative et la formation sur les forêts tropicales. Une illustration concrète du partenariat scientifique Nord-Sud au service de la préservation du patrimoine forestier sous-régional. Cet article Cameroun/ Douala : 80 chercheurs planchent sur l'avenir des forêts du Bassin du Congo est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Paix et vivre-ensemble : la Commission du Bilinguisme convoque les religions à Yaoundé
items.description: © DR La Commission Nationale pour la Promotion du Bilinguisme et du Multiculturalisme organise du 7 au 9 octobre 2026 au Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé un colloque sur le thème « Les religions et la promotion de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre ensemble au Cameroun ». Les religions au cœur de la cohésion nationale.Yaoundé abritera du 7 au 9 octobre 2026 un rendez-vous majeur pour la paix. La Commission Nationale pour la Promotion du Bilinguisme et du Multiculturalisme (CNPBM) organise au Palais des Congrès un colloque sur le thème « Les religions et la promotion de la paix, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre ensemble au Cameroun ». Dans un contexte national marqué par des défis sécuritaires et identitaires, l'initiative entend interroger le rôle des confessions religieuses comme vecteurs de paix, de dialogue et de tolérance. Christianisme, islam et religions traditionnelles seront appelés à partager leurs expériences et leurs contributions à la consolidation du lien social. Pendant trois jours, théologiens, universitaires, autorités traditionnelles, leaders religieux et décideurs publics croiseront leurs regards pour proposer des pistes concrètes en faveur de la prévention des discours de haine, du renforcement du vivre-ensemble et de la préservation de l'unité dans la diversité, socle du multiculturalisme camerounais. Un colloque qui se veut une contribution de la CNPBM à l'apaisement et à la construction d'une nation plus inclusive. Cet article Paix et vivre-ensemble : la Commission du Bilinguisme convoque les religions à Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

VIH pédiatrique : le CNLS évalue l’autodépistage avec le projet DELTA2
items.description: © DR Le Comité national de lutte contre le SIDA participe le 29 septembre 2026 à Yaoundé à l'atelier de dissémination des résultats de l'évaluation du projet DELTA2 sur l'autodépistage du VIH, organisé conjointement avec l'Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation. Une innovation clinique au service du dépistage des enfants. Le Comité National de Lutte contre le SIDA (CNLS) prend part à l'atelier de dissémination des résultats de l'évaluation du projet DELTA2 sur l'autodépistage du VIH, qui se tient à Yaoundé. Les échanges portent notamment sur l'intégration de l'autodépistage du VIH comme innovation clinique visant à améliorer le dépistage et l'identification des cas de VIH chez l'enfant au Cameroun, une cible encore difficile à atteindre dans la cascade de soins. Organisé conjointement par l'Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation (EGPAF) et le CNLS, cet atelier constitue un cadre de partage des résultats, d'échanges d'expériences et de réflexion sur les perspectives d'intégrer l'offre de l'autodépistage assisté dans les stratégies nationales de lutte contre le VIH. L'enjeu est majeur : rattraper le retard du dépistage pédiatrique, lever les barrières socioculturelles et renforcer l'implication des familles. Les recommandations issues de DELTA2 devraient nourrir la prochaine révision des directives nationales. items.title: Lutte contre le trafic de stupéfiants : La Police Nationale saisit près de 86 kilogrammes de cannabis à Ouagadougou
items.description: L’Unité Anti-Drogue de la Direction de la Police Judiciaire (DPJ) a, dans le cadre de la lutte contre le trafic de stupéfiants, mis un terme aux activités illicites d’un réseau de trafic et de vente de cannabis à Ouagadougou. En effet, dans un contexte marqué par l'insécurité et la prolifération des stupéfiants sur l’ensemble du territoire national, elle a intensifié ses actions de lutte contre le trafic et la consommation de drogues dans la ville de Ouagadougou. Ce qui a conduit au démantèlement de ce réseau bien structuré dont les membres s'adonnaient au trafic, à la vente et à la consommation de stupéfiants, de boissons frelatées, de cigarettes de contrebande et de produits psychotropes. Relativement au mode opératoire du groupe, ses membres, qui sont impliqués à divers degrés, effectuaient leur approvisionnement depuis un pays voisin. La marchandise était ensuite acheminée vers Ouagadougou par l’intermédiaire de véhicules de transport en commun ou de véhicules personnels. Une fois à Ouagadougou, elle était stockée avant d’être vendue ou redistribuée à la clientèle. Il est à noter qu’une partie était destinée à des revendeurs et grossistes opérant sur différents sites d’orpaillage à l’intérieur du pays, notamment Boromo et Poura dans la province des Balé, Zanténé dans la province du Sanguié, Sabcé dans la province du Bam, et Mogré et Bittou dans la province du Boulgou. Grâce à la collaboration des populations, les enquêteurs ont, au moment de l’interpellation des membres du réseau, saisi plusieurs objets dont 86 kg de cannabis, des motos, des boissons alcoolisées frelatées, des paquets de cigarettes de contrebande, des plaquettes de produits psychotropes et du numéraire. La Police Nationale remercie encore une fois les citoyens grâce à qui ce résultat a été atteint. Elle invite par ailleurs l’ensemble des populations, particulièrement les parents d’élèves et les responsables des établissements scolaires, à plus de vigilance et à dénoncer tout cas suspect afin de contribuer à préserver l’avenir des plus jeunes. En rappel, les numéros verts que sont les 17, 16 et 1010 sont toujours disponibles et joignables à chaque fois que le besoin se fera sentir. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens !

items.title: Iran court backs 74 lashes for singer who performed without hijab
items.description: An appeals court in Iran has confirmed a sentence of 74 lashes handed to prominent singer Parastoo Ahmadi after she performed without the mandatory hijab, according to her lawyers. Ahmadi, 29, performed in a sleeveless dress during a concert livestreamed on her YouTube channel in December 2024. The performance went viral and attracted millions of views. Iranian law requires women to cover their hair and wear modest clothing in public. Public performances by women are also prohibited. Iran’s judiciary opened proceedings against Ahmadi after the performance, describing it as being “in violation of the country’s legal and cultural regulations”. In June, a criminal court in Qom found Ahmadi and eight members of her band and production team guilty of offences including “offending public decency” through the publication of “obscene and indecent material”. They were sentenced to 74 lashes, a two-year ban on audiovisual activities and a two-year travel restriction. According to their lawyers, a higher court rejected their appeal on Friday without holding a hearing. “In our view, holding the concert was not a crime at all,” one of the lawyers told the BBC. “The trial court imposed one of the harshest punishments for these charges, although fines and less severe penalties were also available.” “The Court of Appeal, despite having the option of holding a hearing, did not hold a hearing and upheld the judgment. It appears that the main reason for issuing this judgment was to deter the recurrence of similar events.” The original sentence sparked widespread criticism, including from Iranian musicians and human rights groups. Exiled singer Googoosh wrote on Instagram: “May these dark days come to an end, and may women regain the freedom to choose how they live and dress, and may artistic expression once again flourish in our precious homeland.” Musician Hossein Alizadeh said he was “willing to take 70 lashes in Parastoo Ahmadi’s place”. Amnesty International also criticised the sentence, saying: “flogging constitutes cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment, and violates the absolute prohibition on torture and other ill treatment”. The case comes amid continued tensions over Iran’s compulsory hijab rules, which became a major focus of nationwide protests following the 2022 death in custody of 22-year-old Mahsa Amini. Since then, many Iranian women have appeared in public without head coverings in defiance of the dress code, while authorities have responded with arrests, warnings and other measures. The post Iran court backs 74 lashes for singer who performed without hijab appeared first on Vanguard News .
